company.text: Pharmasave was founded in **1981** in British Columbia. It is a **member-owned, member-governed co-op** of independent pharmacies: owners sit on regional boards and the national board, and profits go back to members. There are two regional offices: **West** (BC, AB, SK, MB, Yukon) and **East** (Ontario and Atlantic). The national office and Pharmasave West are both in **Langley, BC**. Pharmasave West is a small team (**~35 people**) that supports owners with tools and programs; it is **Great Place to Work certified** (2026 badge). Central programs include the **flyer**, website and app, digital ads, **point-of-purchase (POP) materials, branded shelf signage**, planograms and recommended pricing, plus **700+ private-label (Pharmasave Brand) products**. Stores range from about **500 to 22,000+ sq ft**, so one display rarely fits all. CEO of Pharmasave National: **Ivan Guillen** (since March 2023, ex-Kimberly-Clark and General Mills).

financials.text: Pharmasave is **not listed**, so revenue is not public. **Estimate (not verified):** with 900+ stores, system-wide retail sales are likely in the **several-billion CAD** range, but most of that belongs to independent owners, not the co-op. The marketing budget that matters for Altavia sits in the **regional and national program budgets**, which are not public. Location count: **915** stores as of Oct 9, 2026 (ScrapeHero): Ontario 489, BC 161, Alberta 126, Saskatchewan 51, Manitoba 15, Yukon 1. That makes **~354 stores in the West**.

industry.title: Pharmacy growth is in services, not the front store
industry.text: At Shoppers Drug Mart (Loblaw Q2 2026), pharmacy and services comparable sales grew **7.5%** but the front store grew only **1.3%**. Pharmacies need in-store marketing that works harder to lift front-store sales.

industry.title: Loyalty is the new battleground
industry.text: Pharmasave moved to **BMO Blue Rewards** in June 2026 (800+ participating stores). A Blue Rewards survey says **65%** of people are more likely to pick a pharmacy with a loyalty program. Loyalty promos need consistent in-store signage.

industry.title: Beauty is a strong front-store category
industry.text: Canadian prestige beauty grew **6%** to **$2.2B** in H1 2026 (Circana). Altavia's beauty references (Sephora, L'Oréal, Estée Lauder) are relevant here.

industry.title: Wider pharmacist scope
industry.text: Provinces keep adding services (e.g., Ontario added minor ailments and vaccines in July 2026). New services need in-store communication to be visible.

industry.title: Consolidation pressure
industry.text: Neighbourly Pharmacy (332 stores) and Pharmacy Brands Canada (300+) keep acquiring. Independent banners like Pharmasave must look and execute as well as the big chains.

talking_points: How does your team get a POP or signage program from Langley into ~350 independent stores, and how do you know it went up?
Since each owner is independent, what share of stores actually install a central campaign? Do you measure it?
With stores from 500 to 22,000 sq ft, how do you adapt kits by format today?
How did the Blue Rewards launch go in store? What would you do differently for the next big rollout?
Who prints and ships your materials today: one supplier or several? Is that managed by marketing or procurement?
Where does your team spend the most time: design, approvals, supplier quotes, or store follow-up?
If we found savings or less waste, who besides you would want to see it (Marketing Manager, Director of Marketing, procurement)?
Does East run its own programs, or is POSM shared nationally?

attention.title: Objection: "We have an internal team"
attention.text: He said this up front. Don't pitch design or strategy. Position Altavia as **behind-the-scenes support for his team**: supplier consolidation, production, kitting by store format, and proof of installation. Typical result: **10–15% savings** on print and POSM.

attention.title: Buying authority
attention.text: **Marketing Programs Specialist** is likely not the decision-maker. Use the call to learn the process and ask for an introduction to his manager or the head of marketing at Pharmasave West or National.

attention.title: Co-op complexity
attention.text: Owners are independent and members govern the co-op. Decisions may need board or national sign-off, and the West and East offices may run separate programs. Expect a long cycle.

attention.title: Low Streak scores
attention.text: Streak rates this lead **Fit Low / Interest Low**. Keep the call short and make the goal a referral or a small pilot (e.g., one seasonal campaign in a few stores), not a big deal.
